question.problem:
The matrix $H$ is given below. Let ${h}_{1}$, ${h}_{2}$,  ${h}_{3}$ and ${h}_{4}$ be the respective columns of $H.$
Determine if $B=\text{{}{h}_{1},{h}_{3}\text{}}$ is a basis of $\text{Col}(H).$ 
If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{3}$, where ${h}_{4}={x}_{1}{h}_{1}+{x}_{3}{h}_{3}.$ 

$$
H=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & -6 & 0 & -6 \\ -7 & 18 & -3 & 13\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we reduce the matrix $H$ to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned}H & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & -6 & 0 & -6 \\ -7 & 18 & -3 & 13\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 & -6 \\ -7 & 18 & -3 & 13\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+7{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & 4 & 4 & 13\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 4 & 4 & 13\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-4){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st, $2$nd, and $4$th columns. So, a basis of $\text{Col}(H)$ is $\{{h}_{1},{h}_{2},{h}_{4}\}.$ 

Therefore, we conclude that $B=\{{h}_{1},{h}_{3}\}$ is not a basis of $\text{Col}(H).$
